note: Authoritative local data: GemRadar gems.db (CoinGecko fundamentals + DeFiLlama protocol fees/TVL/revenue) over the longshot.db price/supply/coil backbone. FUNDAMENTALS-FIRST, low-cap gems ($5M-$250M). Raw signals, NO composite score. null = NO DATA (do not guess). Percentiles are sector-relative. coil_lookalikes (longshot winner-DNA) = the TIMING overlay, not the thesis.

coil_lookalikes.method: validated winner-DNA coil screen (deep-below-high + oversold + at-30d-low [all validated, hold OOS] + below-ATH/high-vol/mid-float/small-cap); primed-but-not-yet-moved. NECESSARY-not-sufficient setup — needs an event trigger.
coil_lookalikes.how_to_use: Beaten-down coils matching the data-validated winner DNA. SETUPS, not buys: most never move. Edge comes ONLY from confluence — a lookalike that is also trending / in a heating narrative / has a near catalyst / has fresh dev-gov.

signal_glossary.deep_below_60d_high: Trading <50% of its 60-day high — deeply beaten down. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.oversold_30d: Down >25% over 30 days — oversold. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.at_30d_low: Trading within ~3% of its 30-day low RIGHT NOW — the capitulation launch zone. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample); a bounce off the low actually LOWERS winner odds, so this is a timing edge.
signal_glossary.oversold_90d: Down >40% over 90 days — sustained downtrend (supporting context).
signal_glossary.deep_below_ath: Trading <15% of all-time high — far from prior peak, room to recover.
signal_glossary.high_vol: Elevated 30d volatility — capable of large moves.
signal_glossary.mid_float: Meaningful but not-fully-diluted float — the winner sweet spot.
signal_glossary.small_cap: Sub-$100M market cap — small enough to multiply.

This is a patch release of dcrd which includes the following changes:

- Critical consensus-related security fix
- Prevents a potential periodic deanonymization mixing attack
- Several fixes for potential network-related denial-of-service (DoS) attacks
- Improved mixing session expiry

## Upgrade Mandatory

This release contains a fix for a critical consensus-related security vulnerability.  Everyone is required to upgrade or risk being forked from the network.  This is particularly important for individual stakeholders, Voting Service Providers, PoW miners, and exchanges.

## Changelog

This patch release consists of 23 commits from 3 contributors which total to 20 files changed, 795 additional lines of code, and 392 deleted lines of code.

All commits since the last release may be viewed on GitHub [here](https://github.com/decred/dcrd/compare/release-v2.1.5...release-v2.1.6).

### :exclamation: This release is only to be used as part of the Devnet Automode upgrade process :exclamation:   

   ---   

This Mesa upgrade release contains everything you need to automatically upgrade to the Mesa era on Devnet.
The new approach will allow for much faster and seamless hard forks\upgrades for Mina in future and we are very excited to share it with you!

If you would prefer to handle the upgrade manually (i.e. in two parts), we recommend that you use our [legacy stop slot build](https://github.com/MinaProtocol/mina/releases/tag/3.5.0-devnet-stop-slot). This will require an additional upgrade after the Mesa Devnet netwokr starts; this will be made after the HF takes place. 

For this release we have temporarily enabled node status tracking by default to help us track the successful progress towards the devnet upgrade. This behaviour can be turned off by starting the node using the `--disable-node-status flag`.

For detailed instructions on the upgrade schedule and recommended connection parameters, please refer to our [upgrade documentation](minaprotocol.com/mesa_devnet_upgrade).

### Highlights

- **Revamped documentation** - Comprehensive documentation is now hosted in the emulator repository, check it out [here](https://github.com/cartesi/machine-emulator/blob/v0.21.0/doc/README.md). It features a brand new section on the *verification game*, explaining how the emulator can be used to perform *fraud proofs*.
- **NVRAM address ranges** - Memory ranges can now be exposed in guest userspace memory through the Linux UIO driver. Applications can memory map their state directly onto a machine physical address range, persisting it across advance states efficiently, without any kernel page-cache synchronization overhead.
- **Computation hashes and output proofs** - The Cartesi Machine CLI can now calculate computation hashes over an epoch, track the outputs Merkle tree, write per-output proofs and outputs Merkle root proofs, allowing developers to perform various procedures needed by the Cartesi fraud proof system using just the CLI.
- **Rolling stored machines** - The Cartesi Machine CLI can now advance states using on-disk machines while supporting reverts by cloning stored machine snapshots.
- **Bash completion** - The Cartesi Machine CLI now has bash …[truncated]

## Description

This client release updates polkadot-sdk dependencies to `stable2512` (and the corresponding Frontier version).

**Upgrade priority: HIGH**

Both **collator** and **archive/RPC** nodes must be upgraded alongside [runtime-2300](https://github.com/AstarNetwork/Astar/releases/tag/runtime-2300). Older binaries remain consensus-compatible for a short window, but are **not fully compatible** with the new runtime: EVM tracing (`trace_block`), `XcmPaymentApi` v2, reorg-aware `eth_getLogs`/`eth_subscribe`, and relay-chain collator peer signalling all require this client.

**⚠️ Breaking CLI change:** `--ethapi-trace-cache-duration` (seconds) is replaced by `--ethapi-trace-cache-size` (bytes, default 100MB). The old flag usage must be removed.

Other operator-facing changes:

* New `--trace-filter-max-block-range` flag, defaulting to **1024** blocks (previously unlimited).
* Pre-EIP-155 (non-replay-protected) transactions are now rejected at the RPC layer.
* Frontier mapping-sync now honours the node's state pruning mode.

dev.release_notes:
Celo-Blockchain Release 1.8.9

The latest release sets the `L2MigrationBlock` for Mainnet:

    Block Number: 31056500
    Mar 26th 2025 ~02:43:30 AM UTC

## Bug fixes
 -  Add batch request limit and response size limit in a RPC batch request (#2357 )
 
## Notes
As this is the first Mainnet release from the `v1.8.4` it is worth highlighting the **Notes** from the `v1.8.5`:

> The PR "Omit ethCompatible on RPC responses for non legacy txs (https://github.com/celo-org/celo-blockchain/pull/2302 )" omits also the feeCurrency, gatewayFeeRecipient, and gatewayFee keys from the response when their values are empty. This is to avoid flooding with null information for rpc users that use only Ethereum-compatible transactions.

> Depending on the implementation of the RPC consumers this could be a breaking change. It is done to align RPC output with Ethereum clients in preparation of the L2 launch.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/celo-org/celo-blockchain/compare/v1.8.8...v1.8.9
